You cannot sink in this sea. So why do people keep drowning in it?
The Dead Sea is about ten times saltier than the ocean. The water is so dense, it lifts you like a cork.
But that is the trap. Roll onto your stomach, and the water flips your face down.
Your legs float up, so you can't push your feet down to lift your head.
Swallow a few mouthfuls, and the minerals flood your blood with magnesium and calcium.
Breathe it in, and it burns your lungs from the inside.
Doctors studied 150 near-drownings here. When both lungs were hit, one in four died.
So float on your back, keep your face dry, and never dive in.
